lines.en: I’m so disappointed about the picnic, Lucas. If it hadn’t rained all week, we would have gone to the river, just like we planned.
lines.pt: Estou tão decepcionado com o piquenique, Lucas. Se não tivesse chovido a semana toda, teríamos ido ao rio, como planejamos.

lines.en: Me too. I even packed sandwiches.
lines.pt: Eu também. Eu até fiz sanduíches.

lines.en: That’s the worst part! And I’d already borrowed a tent from my cousin. Do you think the campsite would have been crowded?
lines.pt: Essa é a pior parte! E eu já tinha pegado uma barraca emprestada do meu primo. Você acha que o camping estaria cheio?

lines.en: Probably not. It’s early in the season, so we might have had the whole hill to ourselves. We could have watched the sunset from the top.
lines.pt: Provavelmente não. É começo de temporada, então talvez tivéssemos a colina toda só para nós. Poderíamos ter visto o pôr do sol lá de cima.

lines.en: Stop, you’re making me sadder! Still, if we hadn’t come to the café, we wouldn’t have met those musicians. Did you hear their song?
lines.pt: Pare, você está me deixando mais triste! Mesmo assim, se não tivéssemos vindo ao café, não teríamos conhecido aqueles músicos. Você ouviu a música deles?

lines.en: I did! The guitarist was fantastic. Funny how the day turned out better than I thought, even without the hike.
lines.pt: Ouvi! O guitarrista era fantástico. Engraçado como o dia acabou sendo melhor do que eu pensava, mesmo sem a caminhada.

lines.en: Agreed. Next time, though, let’s check three different forecasts, and book the campsite in spring, so we have a shelter if the weather turns.
lines.pt: Concordo. Mas da próxima vez vamos conferir três previsões diferentes e reservar o camping na primavera, para ter um abrigo se o tempo virar.

lines.en: Good plan. I’m free the first weekend of June, but I’ll be working the one after that. Does that suit you?
lines.pt: Bom plano. Estou livre no primeiro fim de semana de junho, mas vou trabalhar no seguinte. Isso serve para você?

lines.en: Perfect, June it is. If I hadn’t worked last weekend, we could have gone together, but I had to cover a shift.
lines.pt: Perfeito, junho então. Se eu não tivesse trabalhado no fim de semana passado, poderíamos ter ido juntos, mas tive que cobrir um turno.

lines.en: No worries. We’ll make up for it. I’ll bring the sandwiches again, and this time I’ll add a thermos of hot chocolate.
lines.pt: Sem problemas. Vamos compensar. Vou levar os sanduíches de novo e, desta vez, acrescento uma garrafa térmica de chocolate quente.

lines.en: Deal! And since we’re stuck inside today, let’s ask those musicians to play one more song while the rain keeps pouring.
lines.pt: Fechado! E já que estamos presos aqui hoje, vamos pedir àqueles músicos mais uma música enquanto a chuva continua caindo.

facts.big: If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone
facts.label: 3º condicional: planos
facts.sub: If + had + particípio, would have + particípio: If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone. Fala de planos que não aconteceram.

facts.label: se não tivesse + particípio
facts.sub: Use hadn’t + particípio na condição: If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone. A chuva existiu, então o plano não aconteceu. Não use would depois de if.

facts.label: teríamos ido
facts.sub: O resultado usa would have + particípio: we would have gone, we would have seen the sunset. Mostra o que teria acontecido.

compare.ask: If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone.
compare.br: Em português, dizemos “se não tivesse chovido, teríamos ido”.
compare.tip: Diga: “If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use if + past perfect (hadn’t rained) e would have + particípio (would have gone): If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone. O verbo da condição não leva would. O resultado fala do que não aconteceu.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone means we did not go.
We say “If it wouldn’t have rained.”
items.why: We say If it hadn’t rained.

items.s: Would have gone talks about an imaginary result.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone means we did not go. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “If it wouldn’t have rained.” → Falso (We say If it hadn’t rained.)
Would have gone talks about an imaginary result. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A rainy day in Portland · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy Sunday in a park in Portland. Marco and Grace stand under a wooden shelter. Their picnic basket sits on a bench beside them. The river is gray and the trees are dripping. A small group of musicians is setting up nearby. The two friends look at the sky and sigh.

“I am so disappointed about the picnic. If it hadn’t rained all week, we would have gone to the river.” says Grace. “Me too. If the forecast had been right, I would have brought my camera and the new tent.” says Marco. “We would have hiked the whole trail if the ground hadn’t been so muddy.” says Grace.

pages.title: A rainy day in Portland · 3/3
paragraphs: “Then the rain did us a favor. We would have been bored on that long trail anyway.” says Marco. “Maybe! Let us make a plan for next month, and this time, check the forecast together.” says Grace. The musicians begin to play a slow folk song. Grace opens the basket and shares the sandwiches. Marco takes a photo of the rain on the leaves. They write a new date on the calendar app. The clouds slowly open over the hills. A cancelled plan can still turn into a good day.
